captures.description: ATTRIBENCH, BY NAME, ON GOOGLE'S AI OVERVIEW, SIGNED OUT, 2026-10-29: 'The term AttriBench primarily refers to two distinct tools.' First, 'Released in 2026, AttriBench is the first fame- and demographically-balanced quote attribution benchmark dataset for Large Language Models', with its findings (disparities across race, gender and intersectional groups; 'suppression', omission of attribution though the model has the authorship data) and the Hugging Face repository. Second, attribench, a 2023 PyTorch library for benchmarking feature-attribution methods (PyPI, Read the Docs). A note: in finance, AttriBench is a Brinson-attribution exercise. Five cards: arXiv 2604.05224, PyPI, Read the Docs, the bermaneh/AttriBench dataset, Eureka Simulations.

atoms.evidence: Released in 2026, AttriBench is the first fame- and demographically-balanced quote attribution benchmark dataset

Key Findings: Evaluations using this dataset revealed that quote attribution remains highly challenging even for frontier models. It highlighted systematic disparities in accuracy across race, gender, and intersectional groups, as well as a failure mode known as suppression—where a model completely omits attribution even though it possesses the authorship data.

The Purpose: As LLMs are increasingly deployed for search and information retrieval, it is critical that they accurately attribute quotes to their original authors. AttriBench evaluates how well models do this without exhibiting demographic bias.
Availability: The data repository can be explored directly on [Hugging Face]
